proof:
The eroded fiber of the pointwise maximum is exactly the intersection of the eroded fibers for the separate arrays. All such intersections contain a common positive inner homothet for small $\varepsilon$, by bounding the finite maximum of the fields on the original fibers times the sphere. For an anchored representation and input points from the intersections, their barycenter belongs to each separate target, hence to the target intersection. The lifted hull therefore realizes these fibers on the same complete base.

Apply 84cd8a85417b0d7a on each singleton base with the pointwise maximum as the single field; this gives the integral against the actual fixed-cap selector, with the same normal convention and counting measure in dimension one. Define the signed surplus by $R_H(V)=\sum_z\int_{\partial K_z}(\kappa_{z,H}-\beta)V_z(\nu_z,x)\,dS$. Inserting $\max(V,W)=V+W-\min(V,W)$ gives the asserted identity exactly. In particular the correction does not have a fixed sign. If each array has $\sum_z\lambda_z V_z(u,x_z)\ge V_q(u,\sum_z\lambda_zx_z)$ for the old input tuples of each extreme relation, summing these inequalities proves the same sufficient condition for the sum. Applying the defining inequalities at each eroded input point then proves exact compatibility for each extreme relation, and target convexity extends it to every anchored relation.

statement:
Let $P$ be a finite lattice-complete base and $K_z$ positive convex $d$-bodies. Let finitely many arrays of nonnegative jointly continuous fields $V_z^r(u,x)$, convex in $x$ for each unit $u$, each define positive actual compatible fibers for small $\varepsilon\ge0$ by the constraints $u\cdot x+\varepsilon V_z^r(u,x)\le h_{K_z}(u)$. Their pointwise maximum also defines actual compatible fibers, equal to the intersections of the corresponding eroded fibers. Its first total and fixed ambient closed-cap losses use the maximum in the boundary integrals. For two arrays $V,W$ and any real normalization $\beta$, the signed surplus satisfies
$$
R_H(\max(V,W))=R_H(V)+R_H(W)-\sum_z\int_{\partial K_z}(\kappa_{z,H}-\beta)\min(V_z,W_z)\,dS.
$$
Here $R_H$ is first cap loss minus $\beta$ times first total loss, the fields are evaluated at the old a.e. outward normal and boundary point, and the actual cap selector $\kappa_{z,H}$ is one on full traces, zero when the fiber interior is missed, and the strict cap indicator on proper traces. The sum of two arrays is also compatible when both obey the stronger pointwise anchored payment inequality for every extreme relation on the old input tuples.
title: Maxima of compatible support erosions and signed sharing of first losses
